SWFFG.Guide.systeme.preferences.Content:
Game Settings › Configure Settings › Steelers System

Under Interface and shortcuts, open Sidebar icon order. Drag the icons or use the arrows to reorder them. Place the separator between the two groups you want to distinguish.

During an encounter, the banner at the top of the scene shows the active player character’s name or GM’s turn for an NPC. Under Combat and movement, clear Show the combat turn banner to hide it for your account on both ground and space maps.

SWFFG.Guide.pilotage-mj.demande.Content:
GM Control › Request a roll

Choose a skill. The rules panel shows its description, difficulty guidance, and the available reference tables.

Check which connected players should roll, or use All to select everyone who can receive the request. Choose each player’s character and click Send request. The roll window opens for each player so they can prepare and roll their dice.

SWFFG.Guide.systeme.fiches-laterales.Con:
Foundry sidebar › Character sheets

By default, Character sheets sits below Chat. Players see the characters they control and can switch between them with the picker. The GM can pin a sheet with Add a character….

Check the stats, then switch between Skills, Talents, and Equipment. Click a skill to prepare its roll. Use Open chat to jump to the latest visible roll.

The GM can enable this tab in the Steelers System settings. In GM Control, choose where double-clicking a token opens its sheet, either in a standard window or in the Character sheets tab.

SWFFG.Guide.systeme.Title: Steelers - System features
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.Description: Find tools on the full sheet, use the character sidebar, and navigate the system’s directories.
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.module.Title: Enable the core rules
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.module.Content:
Game Settings › Manage Modules

Steelers works fully with the Star Wars FFG - Core Rules FR / EN module (Core Rule Steelers). The system handles sheets and dice rolls. The module provides the rules compendiums, galactic map and travel tools.

As GM, open the world’s module management, enable this module and save. To learn how to prepare a journey, then open the Galactic map and hyperspace travel tour.
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.fiches.Title: Look up talents and configure shortcuts
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.fiches.Content:
Character sheet › Full sheet

On the sheet’s sidebar, the checklist icon opens Talent summary. The lightning bolt opens Trigger a talent and lists talents that have their own action.

The grid icon Shortcuts opens the skill hotbar settings. Choose one of the five pages, then adjust its ten slots before confirming the replacement.

In the sheet’s three-dot menu, Creation and XP opens the advancement guide and Export PDF prepares a printable copy of the full sheet.
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.arbres.Title: Read a talent tree
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.arbres.Content:
Specialization sheet › Talents

The talent trees have been redesigned to make specializations easier to read. Each box shows the talent’s name and XP cost. Lines between the boxes show the available advancement paths.

To plan your next purchase, start from an acquired talent and follow the links to the box you want. To find the text of a talent you already bought during play, return to the character’s Talent summary.
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.repertoires.Title: Choose the right directory
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.repertoires.Content:
Foundry sidebar › Actors · NPC Actors · Vehicles

These three tabs are directories. They all open world sheets. Steelers adds two views to the Actors directory so the GM can find adversaries and vehicles without mixing them with player characters.

Actors
Player characters and other sheets filed alongside them.
NPC Actors
The GM’s view for minions, rivals and nemeses. The GM can right-click to reclassify a character without duplicating its sheet.
Vehicles
World ground vehicles and starships, visible according to each user’s permissions.
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.tonio.Title: Calculate damage with Tonio’s rule
SWFFG.Guide.systeme.tonio.Content:
System Settings › Enable Tonio’s custom rules

This option only changes the damage of a successful attack. The first net success makes the attack hit. Each net success after the first adds one point to the base damage.

Example: a weapon with 6 damage deals 6 damage with one net success, or 8 with three net successes, before soak.
SWFFG.Guide.voyages.Title: Steelers - Galactic map and hyperspace travel
SWFFG.Guide.voyages.Description: Compare routes, prepare or request an Astrogation roll, and record the journey in the starship’s logbook.
SWFFG.Guide.voyages.route.Title: Compare routes
SWFFG.Guide.voyages.route.Content:
Scene toolbar › Galactic map and travel

Click the galaxy icon and choose a Departure and Arrival in the calculator. Compare the routes by duration and off-network segments. The recommended route favors known routes.

Use the Duration multiplier to compare hyperdrives. A value of ×0.5 halves travel time, while ×2 doubles it. The GM can adjust the estimated time for off-network travel.
SWFFG.Guide.voyages.preparation.Title: Prepare the jump
SWFFG.Guide.voyages.preparation.Content:
Galactic map › Prepare journey
  1. Choose the Navigator and Starship. If someone is assisting, select the co-pilot or droid.
  2. Choose the primary or backup hyperdrive, check the duration and supplies, and set the jump conditions.
  3. Click Prepare native roll to open the Astrogation roll on your screen. As GM, click Request a roll to open it directly for the connected player who controls the selected navigator.

The roll window opens with the prepared dice pool for this journey. The player selects their talents and rolls.
SWFFG.Guide.voyages.arrivee.Title: Record the journey’s outcome
SWFFG.Guide.voyages.arrivee.Content:
Chat › Astrogation roll › Journey summary

Everyone can open Journey summary from the Astrogation result in chat. Only the GM can open Resolve journey, set the outcome and any complications, check supplies, and click Confirm journey.

The starship’s Logbook records the departure, arrival, navigator, duration, and outcome of the confirmed journey.
SWFFG.Guide.des.Title: Steelers - Dice rolls and symbol spending
SWFFG.Guide.des.Description: Read a check’s results, spend advantage or threat, and resolve a critical result from chat.
SWFFG.Guide.des.resultat.Title: Read both results of a check
SWFFG.Guide.des.resultat.Content:
Sheet › Skills › Roll › Chat

Click a skill’s dice, check the difficulty, then Roll. In chat, first read the net successes to see whether the action succeeds. Then read any remaining advantage or threat to determine the consequences.

Example: an action can fail while leaving two advantage to spend. A successful action can also generate threat.
SWFFG.Guide.des.depenses.Title: Spend advantage and threat
SWFFG.Guide.des.depenses.Content:
Chat › Roll message › Spend advantage / threat

The system calls negative side effects threat. Beneath the result, open Spend advantage / threat, choose an effect and its quantity. The remaining symbols update before confirmation.

Once confirmed, the expenditure appears beneath the message. Use that expenditure’s undo command to correct a choice. Resolve narrative effects with the GM.
SWFFG.Guide.des.critique.Title: Resolve a Critical Injury
SWFFG.Guide.des.critique.Content:
Chat › Critical expenditure › Resolve critical…

For an attack that can inflict a critical result, select the effect and pay its cost. Then click Resolve critical… beneath the roll. Check the target and modifiers before confirming.

Confirm that the target suffered damage after soak or armor. Choose Roll and apply if you control the target, or Ask the GM otherwise.
SWFFG.Guide.vehicules.Title: Steelers - Vehicles
SWFFG.Guide.vehicules.Description: Get to know the redesigned sheet, assign crew stations, identify owners and track journeys.
SWFFG.Guide.vehicules.tableau.Title: Find your way around the sheet
SWFFG.Guide.vehicules.tableau.Content:
Vehicles directory › Open a sheet

The redesigned sheet groups information by use. The counters at the top show the vehicle’s condition. The Kits and Weapons tab brings together weapons, maintenance and crew. Cargo, malfunctions and the logbook each have their own view.

In combat, start from Kits and Weapons to see who is at each station. Between sessions, start from the Logbook to review the last journey.
SWFFG.Guide.vehicules.equipage.Title: Assign the crew
SWFFG.Guide.vehicules.equipage.Content:
Vehicle sheet › Kits and Weapons › Crew

On an editable sheet, drag a character from its directory onto the Crew table. Use the pencil on its row to choose a station. For a gunner, specify the assigned weapon.

The dice in the row open the check available for that station. The GM can prepare a piloting or gunnery check using the relevant crew member’s skills.
SWFFG.Guide.vehicules.proprietaires.Cont:
Vehicle sheet › Owners & Biography

Drag the character sheet onto the owners list. Click the name to reopen that sheet if you have access. Several characters can own the same starship.

Ownership indicates who owns the vehicle in the fiction. Crew assignments indicate who holds an onboard station. To make an owner the pilot, also assign that station under Kits and Weapons.
SWFFG.Guide.vehicules.journal.Title: Find a hyperspace journey
SWFFG.Guide.vehicules.journal.Content:
Vehicle sheet › Logbook › Journeys

The link is created by selecting the starship’s sheet when preparing a journey on the galactic map. The Astrogation check updates its logbook, and confirmation records the journey’s outcome.

Open a row to see its details. Add a journey lets you record movement manually, such as a trip played without an Astrogation check.
SWFFG.Guide.talents.Title: Steelers - Dice rolls and talents
SWFFG.Guide.talents.Description: Choose an attack’s weapon, apply a talent to a check or trigger a talent’s own check.
SWFFG.Guide.talents.arme.Title: Choose the attack’s weapon
SWFFG.Guide.talents.arme.Content:
Sheet › Combat skill › Rolling

Choose a compatible weapon from the optional weapon list. For a Brawl check you can choose Unarmed. The last weapon choice is remembered for each skill.

Use the target picker to select the token. When attacking, the system automatically upgrades the difficulty according to the target’s Adversary talent rank. Review the pool before rolling.
SWFFG.Guide.talents.associes.Title: Apply a talent to the current check
SWFFG.Guide.talents.associes.Content:
Roll window › Use associated talents

If you control the sheet and an acquired talent offers an action for this check, the Use associated talents button appears before Roll. Open it, read the conditions and select the talent. Check the dice and the stated cost before rolling.

Automation coverage. Not every talent has an implemented mechanic. Its description remains the reference; the player and GM apply any effects that the system does not handle.
SWFFG.Guide.talents.declencher.Title: Trigger or configure a talent
SWFFG.Guide.talents.declencher.Content:
Sheet › Lightning bolt or Talents tab

Some talents trigger their own check. Click the lightning bolt on the right of the sheet and choose the talent. For example, Bad Motivator directly prepares its Mechanics check.

Other talents require a choice first. In the Talents tab, use the cog beside the name when available. For Smooth Talker, choose the relevant social skill and check that it appears beneath the talent.
SWFFG.Guide.pilotage-mj.Title: Steelers - GM Control
SWFFG.Guide.pilotage-mj.Description: Set common difficulty and shared views, request rolls, and run combatants from the sidebar.
SWFFG.Guide.pilotage-mj.commun.Title: Set difficulty and views
SWFFG.Guide.pilotage-mj.commun.Content:
Foundry sidebar › GM Control

Open the sliders icon for GM Control, below Character sheets by default. Set Challenge, Difficulty, and Setback dice, then click Apply difficulty. Check Use for all rolls to apply the common pool.

Use this panel to share the galactic map, market, journal, or portraits. Under Movement and ranges, choose the scene’s movement mode. In Battlemap mode, uncheck Limit movement to keep range bands while letting tokens move freely.

Set range thresholds under Steelers System › Combat and movement › Distances and movement.
SWFFG.Guide.pilotage-mj.individuel.Title: Assign dice to the next roll
SWFFG.Guide.pilotage-mj.individuel.Conte:
GM Control - Combat › Character › Bonuses and penalties
  1. Select the character.
  2. Set Boost or Setback dice, the reason, and the skill for the next roll if needed.
  3. Click Assign. The dice appear when preparing the next matching roll.

The dice are spent when the roll is made. If you close the roll window before rolling, they stay available for the next attempt.
SWFFG.UI.Import.GeneratedNotes:
Importer Notes

This Adversary sheet was imported from OggDude's GMTools with DrMattsuu's NPC importer for SWFVTT, there are currently a number of known issues with this process. 

  • This sheet may be missing alot of data if you skipped the Importing Data step of StarWarsFFG's Getting Started Guide. It is strongly recommended that you follow that guide before attempting to import NPCs/PCs into your game
  • Adversaries do not currently have any of the items created on the Custom Weapons, Custom Armor, or Custom Items tabs of GMTools, this is because those items do not exist in the compendium of imported items.
  • In order for Adversary's Soak values to be displayed properly it is strongly recommended that you disable "Enable Soak Auto Calculation" in the Sheet Options.
  • Adversaries with Force Powers are automatically granted every upgrade in the power-tree they are granted. This is because there's no good way to map the OggDude's exported Adversary force-power upgrades to the SWFVTT character ones.
  • Adversaries Misc. abilities are currently written in the Biography section of the character sheet. This is because the Abilities are not provided in a format that can be easily mapped to Character Abilities.
  • Talents that allow the character to exchange the characteristic used for a skill check (Lightsaber Mastery, for example) are not currently reflected on the character sheet and will need to be manually applied.

SWFFG.UI.Actor.CreationGuideBody:
{name} · Available XP: {available} · Total XP: {total}

Species: {species}
Career: {career}
Specializations: {specializations}

1 · Build the character

  1. Choose the concept, background and group choices (Obligation, Duty or another agreed framework).
  2. Add the species before spending XP: it sets the starting characteristics, abilities and XP budget. Do not drop it onto the sheet repeatedly to receive its XP more than once.
  3. Add an item of type Career, such as Bounty Hunter. A folder named “Bounty Hunter” is not that item.
  4. Add the first career specialization, such as Assassin, by dragging it onto the sheet and choosing Grant. The specialization “+” button opens an advancement purchase.
  5. Choose the free ranks: normally, four different career skills followed by two different bonus skills from the first specialization. Check species exceptions. A career skill checkbox sets the career price; it does not add a rank by itself.
  6. Spend the starting XP, then check wounds, strain, defense and soak, motivations, equipment and appearance. The PC Wizard also offers a fresh creation flow; avoid combining it with grants already made.

2 · Grant or spend XP

Available is the pool remaining to spend. Total is the cumulative amount recorded by the system, not an additional pool. For session rewards, use the GM’s XP grant; directly editing a field is an adjustment that should be checked in the log.

  • Career skill: 5 × the new rank. Non-career skill: the same cost + 5. Buy each rank separately.
  • Characteristic: 10 × the new value, during creation only. Example: 2 → 3 costs 30 XP. At creation, characteristics have a maximum of 5 and skills are limited to rank 2.
  • After creation, improve a characteristic through permitted talents or effects; the available purchase button does not automatically determine the character’s phase.
  • Additional specialization: 10 × the number of specializations after adding it; +10 outside the career. Example: the second career specialization costs 20 XP. Universal specializations follow their own rule, with no surcharge in the code.
  • Tree talents cost 5, 10, 15, 20 or 25 XP according to their row and require the appropriate connections. Owning the tree does not grant all its talents.

Creation or advancement? This guide does not change the character’s phase or automatically validate any choice. A free grant must remain an explicit decision.

Rules checked: Edge of the Empire, pp. 92-93 (PDF 103-104); Age of Rebellion, pp. 102-103 (PDF 103-104). Starting choices: AoR p. 41 (PDF 42).

SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.personal.r: A second maneuver costs 2 strain or replaces the action, unless a specific rule says otherwise. The limit remains two maneuvers during your turn. A lengthy activity may take several turns.
SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.personal.s: Aux Confins de l’Empire, French Core Rulebook, pp. 199-205. Summary of the basic rules; talents, powers and circumstances may modify them.
SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.personal.i: Small tasks that cost neither an action nor a maneuver, within limits set by the GM.
Give an instruction or exchange a few words.
Drop what you are holding or release someone.
Turn around or glance at something. Actual movement requires a maneuver.
Apply the cost, trigger and frequency specified by the ability.
SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.personal.m: Maneuvers
A maneuver normally requires no check. An obstacle or opposition may turn the task into an action.
Move
Change position within short range: 1 maneuver. Short ↔ medium: 1; medium ↔ long or long ↔ extreme: 2. Movement requiring two maneuvers can be spread across several turns.
Engage / disengage
Engage a target at short range: 1 maneuver. Disengage from an opponent: 1 maneuver before moving elsewhere.
Aim
1 maneuver: [BO] on the next combat check; 2 consecutive aim maneuvers: [BO][BO]. Remain in position and attack without another intervening maneuver or action. Damage exceeding soak cancels the aim.
Aim at a specific part
Choose this effect instead of the aim Boost dice: [SE][SE] with 1 maneuver, or [SE] with 2 consecutive aim maneuvers. Agree on the intended effect with the GM.
Assist
Help an engaged ally: [BO] on their next check, used during their next turn. The assistance must be plausible.
Manage gear
Draw, holster, retrieve or stow an accessible item; reload with available ammunition. Each task counts separately.
Interact / take cover
Open a door, operate a control, move an object or reach cover. Ordinary cover gives 1 ranged defense while it actually protects you.
Guarded stance
+1 melee defense and [SE] on your own combat checks until the end of your next turn.
Drop prone / stand up
Each change costs 1 maneuver. While prone: [SE] on ranged attacks against you and [BO] on melee attacks against you.
Mount / take a station
Mount or dismount a trained animal; enter a vehicle or cockpit, or take a firing station. An untrained mount requires an Average [DI][DI] Survival check or harder.
Prepare / fly
Perform the preparation required by a weapon, talent or ability. Personal flight uses appropriate movement; gliding requires a movement maneuver each turn.
SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.personal.a: One main activity per turn. Making a check does not replace its action cost.
Make a combat check with the appropriate weapon and skill. Then spend the results according to the attack’s rules.
Treat an injury, slice a computer, intimidate, climb under pressure or hide from an alert enemy. The GM determines the check and duration.
Spend your action if the ability requires it, even when no check is needed.
Spend the action and resources required by the power, following any exceptions.
Give up the action to perform an additional maneuver, staying within the limit of two maneuvers during your turn.
SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.space.remi: The second pilot maneuver in a round inflicts 2 system strain on a silhouette 1-4 starship. If one pilot performs both, they also pay for their second personal maneuver: 2 strain or their action. Only one pilot action is allowed per starship per round; each other crew member keeps their own turn.
SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.space.sour: Aux Confins de l’Empire, French Core Rulebook, pp. 232-235 and 238, tables 7-2, 7-3 and 7-7. Summary of basic space combat; talents and specific rules still apply. Barrage actions: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook, pp. 246-249.
SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.space.inci: Personal incidentals remain possible when the situation allows them.
Give a heading, report a threat or answer a crewmate. Complex coordination may require an action.
Drop an object, glance at an indicator or perform an incidental granted by a talent. Redirecting shields still requires a maneuver.
SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.space.mane: Both the character’s and the starship’s limits apply. A pilot maneuver concerns the vehicle’s movement.
Increase or decrease speed by 1, between 0 and the vehicle’s maximum.
Move closer, farther away or change position at the current speed. The cost depends on speed and planetary range bands; see the reference below. At speed 0, accelerate first.
Upgrade the difficulty of attacks against the vehicle AND attacks made from it once, until the end of the pilot’s next turn.
Upgrade the ability of attacks made from the vehicle AND attacks against it once, until the end of the pilot’s next turn.
Immediately reach maximum speed. The vehicle suffers 1 system strain per point of speed gained, in addition to any cost for a second pilot maneuver.
Transfer 1 point of defense from one zone to another. Requires access to the controls and defense that can be reassigned.
Aim a turret, manage gear, reach a station or assist an ally: apply personal maneuvers when the situation allows.
SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.space.acti: The gunner, engineer, co-pilot and other crew members can contribute during their own turns.
Use Gunnery or the skill specified by the weapon. Check range and firing arc; difficulty depends on relative silhouettes. A weapon fires only once per round unless an explicit exception applies.

Piloting check: faster than the target [DI]; same speed [DI][DI]; 1 slower [DI][DI][DI]; 2 or more slower [DI][DI][DI][DI]. On success, ignore both vehicles’ evasive penalties and choose the hit zone until the end of the following round. An attempt to regain the advantage gains +1 difficulty for each previous successful gain of the advantage between the two pilots.

Mechanics check: reduce system strain by 1 on a success; repair a Critical Hit at its own difficulty. For hull damage: repair 1 point per success, with only one attempt per encounter, if the repair is feasible. Difficulty depends on the damage level; see the reference below.

SWFFG.UI.CombatReference.Data.space.acti: Average Gunnery [DI][DI]. Silhouette 5+, speed 0-3. All weapons of one type in the chosen arcs fire this round. Until the gunner’s next turn ends, attacking vessels of silhouette 4 or smaller upgrade their combat checks once, plus once per two advantages on the barrage check. Two threats on an incoming check cause a hit for half base damage, rounded up; a despair causes a hit for base damage. The GM determines which approaches are covered.

At least two weapons of one type in the same arc make one normal attack against a silhouette 5+ target. On success, spend one advantage once to add the number of participating weapons to the damage of one hit. All participating weapons have fired for this round.

At least two weapons of one type in one arc make one normal attack. On success, one advantage hits one additional vessel within short range of the original target, plus one vessel per ten weapons. Additional targets must be at least the original target’s silhouette. Repeat the spend if desired, but no vessel can be hit twice by this action. Each additional hit deals base damage plus net successes.
SWFFG.Guide.marche.Title: Steelers - Intergalactic Market
SWFFG.Guide.marche.Description: Find an item, locate a seller and buy with the right character. Understand local prices and market sharing.
SWFFG.Guide.marche.ouvrir.Title: Open the market
SWFFG.Guide.marche.ouvrir.Content:
Scene controls › Store icon

Click the store shortcut on the left, below the galaxy map. The market gathers items from the available compendiums. A catalogue entry does not guarantee that a local seller has it in stock.

If the button is missing, the GM must enable the Steelers Equipment module and Enable the Intergalactic Market in system settings. The Planets module adds worlds and their stopovers.
SWFFG.Guide.marche.catalogue.Title: Find and compare an item
SWFFG.Guide.marche.catalogue.Content:
Market › Categories › Search › Details

Choose a category, enter a name or keyword, then sort by price or rarity. The regulation filter isolates items marked R. Click a row to read its description and statistics in the right panel.

Compare price, rarity and encumbrance. R marks a restriction in the reference profile; the GM determines local legality and required permits.
SWFFG.Guide.marche.lieu.Title: Choose where to shop
SWFFG.Guide.marche.lieu.Content:
Market › Planet › Stopover / port

With the Planets module active, select a suggested planet, then a stopover or port when available. The market displays rarity and price adjustments, along with available stopover services and fees.

Without a location, you are browsing the general catalogue. A market may be closed or unavailable: read its status before searching for a seller. The GM can adjust conditions in Market settings.
SWFFG.Guide.marche.recherche.Title: Find a seller
SWFFG.Guide.marche.recherche.Content:
Item › Find a seller

Choose the character and channel in the right panel. Legal searches use Negotiation. The black market uses Streetwise and applies to restricted items.

Click Prepare the search roll to open the roll window on your screen. As GM, click Request a roll to send the search roll directly to the connected player who controls the selected character.

The GM confirms availability and price before purchase. If the character is missing from the list, the GM can enable market participation in the character’s basic information.
SWFFG.Guide.marche.achat.Title: Buy and browse together
SWFFG.Guide.marche.achat.Content:
Item › Buy · Sidebar › GM Control

Once the sale is agreed, click Buy and review the recipient and amount. Confirming deducts the character’s credits and adds the item to their sheet.

In individual mode, everyone browses their own catalogue. To browse together, the GM opens GM Control in the right sidebar and sets the market’s Shared view and its controller. Use Game rules at the top of the market to check availability rules.
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.Title: Steelers - Space combat map
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.Description: Deploy ships, share the map, move vessels, resolve attacks and track initiative.
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.ouvrir.Title: Enter the space map
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.ouvrir.Conten:
Scene toolbar › Imperial cruiser

Open the map with the Imperial cruiser icon below the market. The hex board fills the scene area. The GM deploys ships by dragging actors from the Vehicles directory onto it. Import compendium vehicles into the world first. The size of each token follows the ship’s silhouette.

Click a ship to show its combat panel on the right. The GM can set Map speed there to deploy the ship at the desired speed without spending a maneuver or suffering strain.
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.partager.Titl: Share the board, keep your camera
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.partager.Cont:
Space map › Round › Shared view

When the GM enables Shared view, all players join the board. Each participant retains their own zoom, camera and selection: a GM camera move does not pan the players’ views.

Disabling sharing closes the map for players while leaving it open for the GM. Outside shared mode, Return to scene takes you back to the previously viewed scene. Personal character shortcuts at the bottom right are hidden while the map is open.
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.equipage.Cont:
Select a ship › Crew and passengers

Players may select ships carrying a pilot, copilot, gunner or passenger they control. The GM can access every vessel. Crew sections start collapsed on selection; the player’s own character sections open for them.

Stations are ordered pilot, copilot, then gunners with their weapons. Passengers have Computers, Mechanics and Leadership. Available controls depend on role and permissions. Click the ship name at the top of the panel to open its full sheet.
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.manoeuvres.Co:
Combat panel › Maneuvers › Fly / Drive

The counter shows pilot maneuvers spent this round. Silhouette 1 to 4 vessels can perform two. Silhouette 5 and larger vessels can perform one. Check the cost shown under the button before confirming.

Choose Fly / Drive, then select a hex in the highlighted area. You can use part of the available distance. Click Confirm to move the ship immediately and spend the maneuver.
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.portees.Title: Read tokens and ranges
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.portees.Conte:
Ship token › Indicators and range button

Token indicators show heading, speed and hull damage. Minion groups also show their number of vessels. The range button helps locate other ships before choosing a target.

Space ranges are Close, Short, Medium, Long and Extreme. Compare displayed distances with your weapon’s range. Right-click a token to reveal the command that brings it to the front when another vessel overlaps it.
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.actions.Title: Fire or use a crew action
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.actions.Conte:
Crew › Fire · Pilot, copilot and crew actions

Click Fire under the station’s weapon. Choose the target ship and facing, then prepare the shot. The system uses the ships’ silhouettes to set Gunnery difficulty and adds setback dice from the target facing’s defense. On a silhouette 5 or larger starship, a weapon marked Anti-fighter defense counts as firing from one silhouette smaller. Check the pool before rolling. Results and resolution controls appear in chat.

Gain the Advantage asks for a target and uses the relative speeds to set difficulty. Co-Pilot is a copilot action. Crew actions include repairs, jamming and scanning. Gunners on silhouette 5 and larger ships can use barrage actions at speeds 0 to 3.
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.rencontre.Tit: Track initiative and the current turn
SWFFG.Guide.combat-spatial.rencontre.Con:
Space map › Round · Sidebar › Combat Encounters

After deploying ships, open Foundry’s Combat Encounters tab. If the board is at Round 0, click Start combat on the board first. The tracker lists characters aboard individually and the ship for integrated stations. Roll Cool or Vigilance for initiative, then start the encounter in the tracker. The GM advances turns and rounds there.

The banner at the top of the map shows the player character’s name, GM’s turn for an NPC or NPC vehicle, or a slot to claim. It follows initiative and disappears when combat ends. To hide it for your account on the space map and other scenes, go to Game Settings › Steelers System › Combat and movement › Show the combat turn banner.

The GM ends the encounter with End combat in the Round menu. The book icon on the map opens Combat turn - vehicles.
SWFFG.Guide.flottes.Title: Steelers - NPC vehicles
SWFFG.Guide.flottes.Description: Choose independent vehicles or NPC profiles and configure minion groups.
SWFFG.Guide.flottes.mode.Title: Choose a vehicle mode
SWFFG.Guide.flottes.mode.Content:
Vehicles › Create or import a vehicle

When creating a vehicle or importing one from a compendium, choose Independent vehicle to assign characters with their own sheets, or NPC vehicle to play it as a single actor with stations and skills stored on its sheet.

For an NPC vehicle, select Minion, Rival or Nemesis, then choose Novice, Standard or Veteran skills. The default is Standard. Set the astromech option to follow the model, always include one or leave it out.
SWFFG.Guide.flottes.postes.Title: Edit integrated skills
SWFFG.Guide.flottes.postes.Content:
Vehicle sheet › Weapons and attachments › Crew and passengers

The pilot, copilot and gunners appear in Crew. From silhouette 4 onwards, the Passengers row groups the support skills Computers, Mechanics and Leadership.

Click the station’s sheet icon to set the ability and rank of its skills. Check Cool and Vigilance at the pilot station to prepare the vessel’s initiative rolls. For a conventional crew, skill values come from the assigned characters.
SWFFG.Guide.flottes.sbires.Title: Configure a vehicle minion group
SWFFG.Guide.flottes.sbires.Content:
Minion NPC vehicle › Scene token › Token sheet

First create a Minion NPC vehicle and place its token on the scene. Open that token’s sheet to set group size. The same model can then support several groups of different sizes.

Counters show total and surviving vessels. Group hull threshold follows group size, and group skill pools decrease with losses. Vehicle minions do not use system strain: those effects inflict hull damage instead. Elimination controls remove a vessel or the group.
SWFFG.Guide.pilotage-mj.combat.Title: Play combatants from one panel
SWFFG.Guide.pilotage-mj.combat.Content:
Foundry sidebar › GM Control - Combat

Open the crosshairs icon. Choose the allied or enemy roster, then narrow the list using search or the initiative, scene, and favorites filters. Single-clicking a token on the scene updates the selected combatant and keeps the current sidebar tab open.

Click an equipped weapon or a skill’s dice to prepare a roll. Talents and equipped weapons and armor appear in the panel. Expand a row for details, or reveal the remaining entries if the list is long. Combat Sheet opens the combatant’s full sheet in combat mode.

SWFFG.CharacterCreator.background.Sugges: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook, p. {page}
Comfortable with Technology
You grew up in a society where droids, starships, and communications networks are part of everyday life.
Isolated Low-Tech World
You grew up in a community apart from the wider galaxy, with little use of modern tools, either by choice or through limited access.
The Privileged Few
You grew up with material security and chances to study or travel that few people around you could afford.
The Poor and Hungry
You learned early to help your household survive. Scarcity shaped how you approach risk and spending.
Ancient Religion
You grew up among people who regarded the Force as an old belief. You may have put the first signs of your affinity down to luck.
Duty to Tradition
Your community recognizes the Force and may train those who are sensitive to it. That training taught you to use your gifts in service of others.
Pragmatic Power
You see your abilities as practical ways to act and reach your goals. Their spiritual significance holds little interest for you.
One with the Force
Teachings about the Force shaped how you understand the world. They guide your decisions and your relationship with the light or dark side.
Fleeing the Empire
Your affinity with the Force drew the Empire’s attention. You left your former life to escape its agents.
Desire for Understanding
You discovered an ability you do not understand. Unable to find answers at home, you set out to look elsewhere.
With Great Power
Seeing the suffering caused by the Empire, you decided to use your gifts to help those in need.
Ultimate Abilities
Your abilities convinced you that you could accomplish great things. You left your former life to develop them and see how far they could take you.

SWFFG.CharacterCreator.StartingTraits.Ob: Aux Confins de l’Empire Core Rulebook, table 2-1, p. 39 (French edition)

An Obligation is a debt, commitment, or problem that can catch up with your character. In Value, enter the points agreed with the GM. A value of 0 means no points have been assigned. Use Description to explain who is involved and what is at stake.
In a group of four PCs, you could split your 10 points into Betrayal 5 and Blackmail 5 if the GM agrees to both origins.

The GM adds up the group’s Obligations and assigns each a range based on its value. At the start of the session, the GM rolls a d100. If it lands in an Obligation’s range, the affected PC’s strain threshold decreases by 2 for the session, and everyone else’s decreases by 1. If a roll of doubles triggers an Obligation, those reductions are 4 and 2. The GM decides how the pressure shows up in the story.
Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook, French edition, pp. 38 to 41. Starting values, table 2-2, p. 40.
